name: telegram
summary: Telegram channel adapter: direct chats, groups and channels over the official Bot API.
help: Connect multiple BotFather tokens to local AI Bots. The Telegram manager discovers chats through one durable collector per token and applies private/group/channel switches plus chat allow or deny lists. Per-room tool grants remain available in advanced channel settings.

The shape of the conversation a message was sent in.

This is a property of the message, not of the binding: one platform account
serves direct chats, multi-party rooms and broadcast channels at the same
time. Four mutually exclusive values cover every adapter surveyed:

- `Direct` — a one-to-one conversation (Telegram private, WeCom single,
  Weixin p2p, QQ c2c, DingTalk type 1, WhatsApp/Signal/iMessage/mail DM).
- `Group` — a named, multi-party, interactive room. Group DMs (Slack MPIM,
  Discord group DM, QQ temporary C2C from a group) and interactive channels
  (Slack channel, Discord guild text, Feishu group) belong here because the
  assistant behaves identically: shared transcript, mention-gated trigger,
  several readers.
- `Broadcast` — a one-to-many surface where posting is restricted to
  owners/admins (Telegram channel, WhatsApp newsletter, Discord
  announcement). The assistant may be unable to reply at all.

Visibility (public vs private) is deliberately *not* a kind: only Slack and
Discord private threads expose it, and no policy branches on it. Threads are
a separate axis carried by the message's `thread` field, never folded into
this enum.

fields.title: Connection
fields.description: Settings for one Telegram bot connection.

fields.title: Account
fields.description:
The bot's own username without `@`, as set in BotFather. Verified
against `getMe` before any message is accepted.

fields.title: Allow Loopback HTTP
fields.description: Permit plain-HTTP `api_base`. Only a loopback host qualifies.

fields.title: API Base
fields.description: Bot API root: the public endpoint, or a self-hosted Bot API server.

fields.title: Bot Token Env
fields.description:
Name of the environment variable holding the Bot API token, never the
token itself: connection settings are stored in the database.

fields.title: Long Poll Seconds
fields.description:
Bounded long-poll window in seconds. Zero answers immediately, which
suits the host's own polling cadence.

fields.title: Credential Kind
fields.description:
`environment` reads the named server variable. `vault` uses a write-only
token stored separately through the host plugin secret store.

The installed adapter verifies these facts with its platform. A user
cannot obtain membership just by putting an ID/role in message text.
